summary:
**SPACE LEGACY – Abandoned But Not Forgotten**

SPACE LEGACY is a free, interactive digital space museum designed to preserve and share the stories of NASA's historic space missions and abandoned equipment.

Information about old spacecraft, rovers, landers and scientific instruments is scattered across different websites, making it difficult for young learners to explore their history in one place. SPACE LEGACY addresses this problem by bringing space exploration stories together in an engaging digital platform.

The project includes a Space Heritage Archive, interactive 3D mission exhibits, Knowledge Quest (a space science quiz) and Play & Learn (a code-based rover exploration game). These features help users discover historic missions, explore equipment, learn scientific facts and test their knowledge.

Built using HTML, CSS, JavaScript, Three.js, WebGL and Rapier physics, SPACE LEGACY aims to make space education accessible, interactive and enjoyable.

The platform is intended for students, teachers, space enthusiasts and educational institutions. It will remain completely free, with potential future support through educational partnerships, sponsorships and grants.

**Our vision: Even when a mission ends, its legacy should never be forgotten.**
details:
SPACE LEGACY

Theme: Abandoned But Not Forgotten

1. Project Overview

SPACE LEGACY is a free, interactive digital space museum that preserves and presents the stories of historic NASA spacecraft, rovers, landers and scientific equipment left behind on the Moon and Mars. It brings space exploration history, engineering and scientific discoveries together in one educational platform.

2. Problem Addressed

Information about historic space missions and abandoned equipment is spread across multiple websites. Students often need to switch between different sources to understand a mission, its equipment and its discoveries. Long, text-heavy information can also make learning less engaging.

3. Proposed Solution

SPACE LEGACY provides a centralized platform where users can discover, explore and learn about historic space missions through interactive features.

4. Main Features

  • Space Heritage Archive: A homepage introducing the Moon, Mars and historic missions, including Apollo 15 Lunar Roving Vehicle, Surveyor 3, Spirit and Opportunity.
  • 3D Mission Archive: Interactive 3D exhibits featuring NASA mission equipment such as Ingenuity, InSight, Viking landers and Spirit/Opportunity rovers.
  • Knowledge Quest: A space science quiz with 25 levels, five stages, XP points and level progression. Users need at least 7 correct answers out of 10 to unlock the next level.
  • Play & Learn: A code-based rover exploration prototype featuring Moon and Mars environments, rover controls, scanning, discoveries, science data and expedition objectives.

5. Technology Used

HTML5, CSS3, JavaScript, Three.js, WebGL, Rapier physics, model-viewer, LocalStorage, external 3D assets and CDN-hosted libraries. Development tools include Visual Studio Code, Live Server and Chrome.

6. Target Audience

School students, college students, teachers, young space enthusiasts and educational institutions. The Play & Learn game is primarily intended for learners aged 8 and above.

7. Accessibility and Sustainability

SPACE LEGACY is planned as a completely free educational platform, without subscriptions or paid access. Potential future support may come through educational partnerships, sponsorships, voluntary donations and grants.

8. Project Vision

To make space exploration history easier to discover, understand and experience, while preserving the engineering achievements and scientific legacy of missions that have ended.

Even when a mission ends, its legacy should never be forgotten.
